=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## 0. Threshold point: the Seller's framing

The preamble asserts that these positions are "market", were "settled at principal level", are "FINAL" and "not intended to be re-opened". That is the other side's advocacy, not a fact we should accept. Please confirm with the Wattlebridge principals what (if anything) was actually agreed commercially. Even if a 20% cap / 1% basket / 18 months was agreed in headline terms, several of the detailed positions below (fundamental warranties capped, Riverlark released *after* Completion, bonuses outside the funds flow, buyer-knowledge bar) go well beyond any normal headline agreement and should be treated as open. Our mark-up should respond on the merits and not be anchored by the "FINAL" label.

More importantly, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter admits a series of live, unquantified problems (Bluefen consent not obtained, Riverlark not repaid, Ironquay IP not paid for, bonuses not in funds flow, a privacy incident under investigation). The limitation package is drafted so that, in combination, almost all of these would be unrecoverable: general disclosure of the data room (Sch 7) + buyer-knowledge bar including "discoverable" matters (cl 8.3) + all Claims subject to the general cap/time limits (cl 12.3, 9.3/12.8/20.5) + the Ironquay indemnity narrowed to a payment amount. The package needs to be assessed as a whole, not clause by clause.

---

## 1. Liability regime (cl 12, 13)

**1.1 General cap – 20% (AUD 4.8m).** Negotiable rather than unacceptable, but low for a sub-scale SaaS target with known issues and a VC seller that will likely distribute proceeds. Push for 30–50%; fall-back is 20% only if paired with (a) separate uncapped/price-capped fundamental warranties, (b) separate caps for tax, IP and the specific indemnities, and (c) a retention/escrow or W&I policy. Also check Seller's covenant strength – Harbourglass is a VC vehicle; require a parent/fund guarantee or escrow (10–15% of price for the claims period).

**1.2 Fundamental/title warranties under the general cap and 18 months.** Reject outright. Capacity, authority, title to shares, no encumbrances, share capital – must be capped at 100% of price and run for at least 6 years (statutory limitation period). "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to give away recourse if we have not acquired what we paid AUD 24m for.

**1.3 Thresholds (cl 12.2).** De minimis AUD 25k (~0.1%) is acceptable. Basket AUD 250k (~1%) is at the upper end; push for 0.5% and, critically, make it a **tipping** basket (recover from first dollar once exceeded) not a deductible. Carve out from both thresholds: fundamental warranties, tax warranties/indemnity, the specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses, Riverlark), leakage/debt-free adjustments, and fraud.

**1.4 Time limits (cl 12.3/13).** 18 months is short – it does not give the Buyer two post-Completion audit cycles. Seek 24 months for general warranties; 7 years for tax (ATO amendment periods plus buffer); 6 years for fundamental; IP warranties at least 36 months. Claims notified in time should survive if proceedings commenced within 6–9 months. Reject the "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" default – it reverses the drafting burden and will sweep in indemnities, covenants and completion mechanics.

**1.5 Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature".** Reject. Must carve out: fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment; the specific indemnities; the debt-free/cash-free price adjustment and leakage claims; pre-Completion covenants (conduct of business); title. Non-reliance clause should not exclude the Disclosure Letter responses, management presentation and written DD responses on which the Buyer is relying, and cannot exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under the ACL in any event (s 18 cannot be excluded – worth noting in the mark-up so the clause is not drafted to overreach).

**1.6 Tax and IP "settled under the general regime".** Not acceptable. Require a standalone tax indemnity/covenant (pre-Completion tax, full price cap, 7 years, not subject to disclosure or basket) and a separate IP cap given the Ironquay issue.

---

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

**2.1 Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2 – general disclosure of the entire data room and "publicly searchable corporate records".** Push back hard. The standard should be matters **fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter**. Delete general disclosure of public records entirely (or limit to specified ASIC/PPSR/court searches against the Company at a fixed date, with copies annexed). A fixed, indexed data room schedule should be attached, not "the data room as at 5pm 22 Sept 2026" (we should also check whether anything was uploaded late).

**2.2 Clause 8.3 – Buyer knowledge, including advisers and anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.** This is the most dangerous single clause. It is a constructive-knowledge bar: anything that *could* have been found anywhere defeats a claim, regardless of fair disclosure. Combined with 2.1, the warranties become near-worthless. Replace with a pro-sandbagging provision: Buyer's knowledge (actual or imputed) does not affect any Claim, save for matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter against the relevant warranty. At minimum, confine to actual knowledge of named Buyer individuals and delete "discoverable", "advisers" and "public records".

**2.3 Disclosure Letter 1.4 (no admissions) and 11 (reservation).** Acceptable in themselves, but note the tension: the Seller discloses problems while refusing to characterise or quantify them. That transfers risk assessment to us – hence the need for specific indemnities rather than reliance on disclosed warranties.

---

## 3. Transaction-specific issues

**3.1 Bluefen (cl 3/6.3; DL 2) – ~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue; change-of-control consent not obtained; conditions under cl 11.3 not satisfied.** The Seller's position ("reasonable endeavours", consent "treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent") is inadequate.
- Make Bluefen consent a **Condition Precedent** to Completion, in a form reasonably satisfactory to the Buyer, with written evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions have been satisfied or waived, and without any adverse variation to pricing, term or scope.
- Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours** and keep Buyer informed; Buyer to have participation rights in communications with Bluefen.
- Buyer termination right if not satisfied by the Long Stop Date; consider a price reduction or retention mechanic if Bluefen reduces scope or terminates within 12 months.
- Warranty that no other customer contracts contain change-of-control rights beyond those listed.

**3.2 Riverlark Bank (cl 2/7; DL 3) – ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control default (cl 8.1); release "to be provided following Completion".** Unacceptable on a debt-free/cash-free deal.
- Repayment must occur **at Completion** out of the purchase price via the funds flow (payoff letter from Riverlark fixing the payout figure; direction to pay).
- **Completion deliverables:** executed deed of release, PPSR discharge/financing change statements, release of any guarantees, return of title documents. Not a post-Completion promise.
- Confirm the AUD 3.2m (plus break costs, accrued interest, fees) is reflected as Debt in the price adjustment; Seller indemnity for any residual amount.
- Confirm that change-of-control under cl 8.1 does not trigger any event of default before repayment on the Completion date.

**3.3 Closing bonuses (DL 5; funds flow) – AUD 420k, excluded from funds flow, on-costs unknown.** These are transaction-related costs triggered by Completion; on a debt-free/cash-free basis they are a Seller cost (Transaction Bonuses/debt-like item), not an ordinary operating expense of the Company post-Completion.
- Include in the funds flow or deduct from price, **grossed up** for superannuation guarantee, payroll tax, PAYG and any leave accruals.
- The continued-employment condition means the Company will be paying after Completion – Seller to fund through price deduction or indemnify; Buyer to control payment timing and messaging.
- Obtain copies of the bonus letters; check for retention/termination rights and whether any bonus is to the Seller's own nominees.

**3.4 Ironquay (cl 11.1; DL 4) – SOW3 Project Materials do not transfer until all SOW3 fees are paid; AUD 180k open; no assignment on file; indemnity limited to the AUD 180k payment.** This is an IP-ownership gap in what is, presumably, part of the product. The Seller's "adequate" indemnity covers only the invoice, not the consequence (Company does not own code it is selling).
- **Completion deliverables / CP:** proof of payment of all SOW3 fees and an executed confirmatory IP assignment and moral rights consent from Ironquay (and its personnel) in favour of the Company.
- DD: identify exactly what SOW3 materials are and whether they are embedded in the platform; check SOW1/SOW2 for similar conditions.
- Specific IP indemnity: full price cap (or at least separate cap), 36+ months, covering third-party claims, licence fees, re-development costs and loss of revenue – not limited to the open invoice.
- Reinforce IP warranties (sole ownership of all platform IP, no open-source copyleft contamination, all contributors have assigned).

**3.5 Export/privacy incident (cl 4.6/Sch 6; DL 6) – ~1,240 records of personal information sent to an unintended external recipient; investigation preliminary; notification position unresolved.** "Not expected to be material" is not a basis for the Buyer to take the risk. Under the Privacy Act NDB scheme this may be an eligible data breach; it may also breach confidentiality terms in customer contracts (including Bluefen).
- Seller to complete the investigation and reach a documented notification decision **before Completion**; Buyer to review and approve; OAIC/affected-individual notifications (if required) to be made pre-Completion.
- **Specific indemnity** – separate cap (at least 25–50% of price), 3–4 years, no basket/de minimis – covering regulatory penalties, remediation, customer claims and credits, notification costs.
- Warranties: no other incidents; compliance with APPs; adequate security program; conduct-of-business covenant to notify Buyer of any further incidents.
- Make it a representation that the DD-006 disclosure is complete and accurate as at Completion.

**3.6 Sandbar renewals (DL 8; DD-008/DD-011) – three related renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k).** Three identical amounts "read together" suggests a commitment split below a threshold. Verify: counterparties/related parties, whether the renewals were signed before or after the locked-box/accounts date, term and termination rights, whether any is for services not needed post-Completion. If committed outside the ordinary course for the Seller's benefit, treat as leakage/debt-like. Conduct-of-business covenant: no new contracts/renewals above a threshold (e.g. AUD 50k p.a.) without Buyer consent; aggregation anti-avoidance language.

**3.7 Office lease (DL 7) – notification obligation.** Low risk, but Seller to procure the notification is given (and acknowledged) before Completion, with confirmation that no landlord consent or guarantee re-issue is required.

**3.8 Mossvale (DL 9) – restriction on assignment.** A share sale is not an assignment, so the Seller is probably right, but have DD confirm there is no separate change-of-control or "deemed assignment" wording, and obtain a warranty that no counterparty consents are required other than Bluefen.

**3.9 Title (DL 10; DD-012).** A share register is only prima facie evidence (Corporations Act s 176). Buyer DD to verify: current ASIC extract, constitution (pre-emption/transfer restrictions), PPSR searches against the Company and the Seller (share security to Riverlark?), no options, convertible notes, ESOP rights or shareholder agreements. Title warranties uncapped, 6 years, not qualified by disclosure.

---

## 4. Summary of recommendations (in priority order)

1. **Do not accept the "FINAL / market" framing.** Confirm with principals what was agreed; respond on the merits.
2. **Carve fundamental, title and tax warranties out of the general regime** – 100% price cap, 6–7 years, no basket, no disclosure qualification.
3. **Delete cl 8.3 constructive knowledge bar and the "all Claims of any nature" sweep in cl 9.3/12.3/12.8/20.5**; carve out fraud, indemnities, price/leakage mechanics and pre-Completion covenants.
4. **Replace general disclosure** with a "fairly disclosed" standard against an indexed, fixed data room; delete public-records disclosure.
5. **Bluefen consent as a Condition Precedent** (satisfactory form, cl 11.3 conditions evidenced), with termination right.
6. **Riverlark repaid and released at Completion** via funds flow with deed of release and PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables; reflected as Debt.
7. **AUD 420k bonuses plus on-costs borne by Seller** – in funds flow or price deduction.
8. **Ironquay:** payment and confirmatory IP assignment as Completion deliverables; broaden the IP indemnity.
9. **DD-006 incident:** investigation and notification decision closed out pre-Completion; standalone indemnity.
10. **Improve the general regime** – cap 30–50% (or 20% with escrow/W&I), tipping basket at 0.5%, 24 months – and secure Seller credit via escrow/guarantee.
11. **DD follow-ups:** Sandbar renewal terms and timing; Mossvale change-of-control wording; independent title verification; SOW1/2 IP terms.

I can turn this into a clause-by-clause mark-up or an issues list for the deal team call if useful.
